checks: Read the exact claim and proof first, then compared 61c2a6c203bcade2 §§1–4 and 85a041ec649c5375 §§7–9. The extension to neighborhood-defined fields and the normal-independent closure have the stated scope.

Each affine gap is nonnegative on the full original hull, since it is nonnegative on every generating fiber. Compact index maximization, positive part, and the uniform bound on the fields give convexity and decreasing bounded penalty traces on that hull.

For each fixed penalty, subgradients on a compact convex thickening are bounded by local convex Lipschitz bounds. Their supporting affine envelope, with zero included, is finite everywhere and agrees on the thickening. Extending orthogonally causes no change in the relative geometry.

The zero-gap condition is the sum of two nonnegative equalities and hence identifies the unique old normal at a regular point. Maximizers along increasing penalty have gap at most B/L and limit to old contacts. Dominated convergence then gives the L1 bound and its uniformity over bounded boundary tests.

The roof formula uses the actual sections of the lifted hull. Mixing coefficient vectors gives concavity and compactness gives upper semicontinuity in the real base, so the constraints are convex and closed. The inner homothets keep every sampled fiber positive and keep projection equal to the old base hull.

Taking the same field on each continuous affine majorant gives exact equality of measured sections for each parameter, because the minimum of the majorants is the old support on sampled bases. The finite radial formula then applies including pure-base and inside/outside supporting traces.

For a strict finite margin choose one finite penalty first, then use the first-order remainders for that fixed deformation. Continuity of each finite response map gives both closure inclusions and the same polar inequalities.

dependencies.hypotheses: For each original p, the compact convex fibers satisfy the anchored inclusion whenever the coefficient vector represents p. The resulting continuous affine support majorants all dominate the old measured supports, and the p-plane touches at p for every unit normal.

The original action restricted to C and the same-field action on touching planes satisfy the finite, nonnegative, jointly continuous convex field and support ceiling hypotheses. The radial limit, inner homothet, and all fixed-cap selectors apply on the complete finite base, including endpoint counting in d=1.

overlap.comparison: This gives exact finite addition within the contact-action class. It has no reduction to a single normal-independent convex potential or approximation of all such responses.
This gives the contact radial speed and fixed cap derivatives. The penalty extension, L1 limit, and roof-to-action converse are additional.

readability: The exact converse concerns the integer sections. The proof does not need equality of the ambient bodies at real unsampled bases, or uniform remainders in L.
review_method: Independent cold proof read of the frozen input, original source comparison, predecessor checks, and direct derivation or exact arithmetic replay where applicable.
summary: The penalty yields a single global convex potential whose physical trace converges in boundary L1. The roof is an actual nested deformation, and touching planes give the reverse realization on every measured fiber.
